english.note: This is the everyday all-purpose choice for calling someone mean or unkind, though it can also simply mean bad.

exampleSentences.english: The way you treated that old person was really unkind.
exampleSentences.traditional: 你咁樣對個老人家，真係好衰。
exampleSentences.jyutping: nei5 gam3 joeng2 deoi3 go3 lou5 jan4 gaa1 zan1 hai6 hou2 seoi1

english.note: For an unkind person or action, this is the all-purpose spoken choice; it can also describe something shabby, inferior, or malicious.

exampleSentences.english: The way they treat people is really mean.
exampleSentences.jyutping: keoi5 gam3 joeng2 deoi3 jan4 zan1 hai6 hou2 seoi1

english.note: Use this for a person or behaviour that is mean, nasty, or treats someone badly, rather than for physical shabbiness.

exampleSentences.english: That was shabby of you, taking someone else’s credit as your own.
exampleSentences.traditional: 你咁衰，竟然攞人哋份功勞當自己嘅。
exampleSentences.jyutping: nei5 gam3 seoi1 ging2 jin4 lo2 jan4 dei6 fan2 gung1 lou4 dong1 zi6 gei2 ge3

english.note: Use this for a person or their behaviour when they are contemptible, mean, or unkind.

exampleSentences.english: You’re being really nasty talking about people.
exampleSentences.jyutping: nei5 gam2 joeng2 gong2 jan4 zan1 hai6 hou2 seoi1

english.note: Use 衰 for a person who is mean, cruel, morally bad, or generally lousy.

exampleSentences.english: They are so rotten that they even cheat old people.
exampleSentences.jyutping: keoi5 gam3 seoi1 lin4 lou5 jan4 gaa1 dou1 aak1
